A pre-82 $0.01 is worth ~$0.017 or nearly twice its face value vs. melt. A nickel OTOH is only worth 80% of face (which is better than any other coin except the pre-81 penny.) If gold skyrockets, nickel & copper may get dragged up as well. What could you do with pennies/nickels if things get so bad that hedge metals are a good idea; who might accept them in trade? Likely most would view them at face value only so if fiat money (US dollar) crashes you'd be stuck trying to explain their inherent base metal value vs. face value and that they were really worth more. In other words you may be stuck with something tough to extract any value from at all and is heavy in any quantity.

Silver and especially pre-64 coinage is usually understood to have inherent value beyond face value even with younger people. I believe your chances to use it would be much better.
